knowledge_point.title: Finding Particular Solutions of Differential Equations by First Rearranging and Then Separating

question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{4{y}^{2}}{{(x + 2)}^{2}}+{y}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={y}^{2}(\frac{4}{{(x + 2)}^{2}}+1) \\ \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & =(4{(x + 2)}^{-2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int {y}^{-2}\,\text{d}y & =\int (4{(x + 2)}^{-2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\ -{y}^{-1} & =-4{(x + 2)}^{-1}+(x + 2)+C \\ -\frac{1}{y} & =-\frac{4}{(x + 2)}+(x + 2)+C\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $y$, we find the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{y} & =\frac{4}{(x + 2)}-(x + 2)-C \\ \frac{1}{y} & =\frac{4-{(x + 2)}^{2}-C(x + 2)}{(x + 2)} \\ y & =\frac{(x + 2)}{4-{(x + 2)}^{2}-C(x + 2)}\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(0)=-1$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) & =-1 \\ \frac{2}{4-{2}^{2}-C(2)} & =-1 \\ \frac{2}{-2C} & =-1 \\ -\frac{1}{C} & =-1 \\ C & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the particular solution is

$$
y(x)=\frac{(x + 2)}{4-(x + 2)-{(x + 2)}^{2}}.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{e}^{-y}=4{(x - 4)}^{3}{e}^{-y}$ that satisfies $y(5)=0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{e}^{-y} & =4{(x - 4)}^{3}{e}^{-y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4{(x - 4)}^{3}{e}^{-y}-{e}^{-y} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(4{(x - 4)}^{3}-1){e}^{-y} \\ {e}^{y}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =4{(x - 4)}^{3}-1 \\ \int {e}^{y}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (4{(x - 4)}^{3}-1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int {e}^{y}\,\text{d}y & =\int (4{(x - 4)}^{3}-1)\,\text{d}x \\ {e}^{y} & ={(x - 4)}^{4}-(x - 4)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the natural logarithm to both sides, we find the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({(x - 4)}^{4}-(x - 4)+C) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({(x - 4)}^{4}-(x - 4)+C)\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(5)=0$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(5) & =0 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{4}-1+C) & =0 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡C & =0 \\ C & =1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{e}^{-y}=4{(x - 4)}^{3}{e}^{-y}$ that satisfies the condition $y(5)=0$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡({(x - 4)}^{4}-(x - 4)+1).
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation ${e}^{(x + 4)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-2(x + 4){e}^{(x + 4)}=3$ that satisfies $y(-4)=-3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{(x + 4)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-2(x + 4){e}^{(x + 4)} & =3 \\ {e}^{(x + 4)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3+2(x + 4){e}^{(x + 4)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{e}^{-(x + 4)}+2(x + 4) \\ \int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3{e}^{-(x + 4)}+2(x + 4))\,\text{d}x \\ \int \,\text{d}y & =\int 3{e}^{-(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x+\int 2(x + 4)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =-3{e}^{-(x + 4)}+{(x + 4)}^{2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(-4)=-3$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-4) & =-3 \\ -3{e}^{-0}+{0}^{2}+C & =-3 \\ C-3 & =-3 \\ C & =0\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of ${e}^{(x + 4)}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-2(x + 4){e}^{(x + 4)}=3$ that satisfies the condition $y(-4)=-3$ is

$$
y={(x + 4)}^{2}-3{e}^{-(x + 4)}.
$$
